newsitem.title: USA: Allergan sees lower first half earnings.
newsitem.headline: Allergan sees lower first half earnings.

text.p: Allergan Inc said it expects earnings for the first half of 1997 to be as much as 20 percent lower than the $0.80 per share earned in the first half of 1996.
Earnings in the year-ago first half excluded the impact of special charges.

Allergan said the expected decline this year is due mainly to launch expenses for new products, "continuing competitive pressures" on the eye care business, as well as the impact of foreign currency fluctuations.
The company said it is proceeding with a restructuring program adopted last June to streamline operations and reduce cost structure to help fund new product launches.

It said the initial acceptance in the U.S. of its Alphagan treatment for open-angular glaucoma and ocular hypertension is ahead of plan and it is pursing additional product approvals that could benefit second half results.
The consensus estimate by analysts is for earnings in the first half of $0.83 per share, according to First Call.
